title: C256 — Passenger airbag connector
introduction:
I start with the cavity label, then read across its circuit row. That matters here because a wire color can appear on more than one assigned circuit: color is a useful clue, but a poor name tag on its own.

The identification table establishes which connector this sheet describes. The drawing links cavity locations to the assignment table, whose Function entries distinguish the signed passenger-airbag connections and adaptive-venting connections. Preserve each function’s positive or negative designation when reading. Shaded drawing positions correspond to rows without circuit assignments; they are not, by themselves, evidence of missing wiring.

The final table is a pigtail catalog reference. Physical viewing direction, gauge convention and the meanings of Box, Cols and Size are unspecified. Neither the drawing nor the catalog supplies access, terminal-release, repair or test instructions. This guide supports understanding the labels; hands-on restraint work requires the separate safety and service procedures.

items.name: Qualified personnel and prescribed procedures
items.detail: Pyrotechnic-component service is restricted to qualified personnel. Hands-on work requires the matching restraint-specific depowering, handling, specified test equipment and restoration sequence, which this connector reference does not teach. See [Pyrotechnic Device Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693191).

items.name: No improvised electrical tests
items.detail: Do not substitute a generic jumper or resistance test for the prescribed restraint diagnostic method. Connector assignments alone do not establish a permitted test.

edits.why: The displayed drawing has a vertical line of cavities with the projecting housing structure on the left. Those features help locate labels within the illustration. They do not establish the physical viewing side or show how to release the connector or its assurance mechanism.

I keep Cavity, Circuit Number and Function together so similar colors cannot blur distinct airbag and adaptive-venting connections. The signs belong to the named functions; they are not instructions to apply power. The adaptive-venting negative row lacks a usable terminal part number. Leave that catalog gap unresolved rather than copying an adjacent terminal entry.

The pigtail is the connector-and-lead service assembly. Match Kit List to Number and compare Hard Shell with Engineering Shell to understand the catalog relationship. Service Part and Terminal Part Number refer to different items. A pigtail listing does not authorize a restraint-wiring repair or supply the required connection and verification sequence.
